147.05700,-19.27600.desc: Breeds and conditions corals and their symbiotic algae for heat tolerance, and works on engineered symbionts. Anything put on a reef is released into open water that connects to every other reef, so there is no containment available even in principle — and the alternative being weighed against it is the reef dying.

116.40740,39.90420.name: Sinogene Biotechnology
116.40740,39.90420.desc: A commercial pet-cloning company that also clones for the police. It sells copies of dead pets at around fifty thousand dollars, and separately produced Kunxun, China's first cloned police dog, from a Kunming wolfdog credited with helping solve twelve murder cases — work done with Yunnan Agricultural University and the support of the Ministry of Public Security. In November 2019 six cloned dogs were sworn into the Beijing police, their DNA more than 99 per cent identical to two Belgian Malinois chosen for their record on the force. The economic case is training rather than biology: conventional training runs about five years and up to half a million yuan with no guarantee of success. The company's own scientist concedes clones share appearance and general health but that upbringing may still make behaviour differ, and a veterinarian quoted alongside notes China has no animal protection law under which pet cloning could be regulated. The surrogate mothers that carry these pregnancies are the part of the service that has no customer.

116.40740,39.90420.name: JOINN Laboratories
116.40740,39.90420.state: Beijing — with Suzhou, Chongqing, Guangzhou and US sites
116.40740,39.90420.desc: Founded in 1995 and listed in both Shanghai and Hong Kong, this is the largest non-clinical safety assessment provider in China: 73,200 square metres of animal experiment facilities across its two main bases alone, holding accreditations against Chinese, US, OECD, Japanese and South Korean good laboratory practice, and expanded into the United States by acquisition. Its dedicated laboratory animal sites sit separately in Wuzhou, Yunnan and Nanning. Two things follow. Safety studies read by regulators worldwide are increasingly produced in a country the reading regulator does not inspect — the accreditations are the substitute for that. And the company moved to secure its own primate breeding capacity when the supply tightened, so the contractor running the study and the supplier of the animals used in it are converging into one firm.

116.40740,39.90420.name: Vital River Laboratories
116.40740,39.90420.state: Beijing — Charles River joint venture in China
116.40740,39.90420.desc: The Chinese joint venture of the largest laboratory animal supplier in the world, providing research animal models and related services into the domestic biopharmaceutical sector. A joint venture is a particular arrangement worth recording rather than glossing: the foreign partner gets a route into a market that restricts direct entry, the domestic partner gets the breeding lines and the standards, and the resulting animals are neither wholly one company's nor the other's on any register a reader can consult. The engineered strains this map tracks elsewhere by repository catalogue move through structures like this one without a catalogue.

116.40740,39.90420.name: China Animal Husbandry Industry Co. (CAHIC)
116.40740,39.90420.desc: A state-backed producer and, on one 2015 measure, the largest single share of the Chinese animal vaccine market. Its portfolio covers the diseases the state designates as priorities — foot-and-mouth, highly pathogenic avian influenza, classical swine fever — and its government relationships, national distribution and production scale are what make it structural rather than merely large. The mechanism worth carrying: China divides animal vaccines into compulsory and market-priced categories, and the compulsory list is set by the state. A government deciding which diseases must be vaccinated against is deciding the size of a market, and this is the company positioned to serve it.

77.24000,28.62240.name: Aruna Rodrigues v Union of India
77.24000,28.62240.state: New Delhi — Supreme Court of India
77.24000,28.62240.desc: A public interest petition filed in 2005 and still running. Its record is the longest continuous judicial supervision of engineered crops anywhere: the Court directed the regulator to withhold approvals in September 2006, lifted that in May 2007 subject to a 200 metre isolation distance around field tests, added a 0.01 per cent level-of-detection protocol in April 2008, appointed an independent expert in 2009, and in 2012 appointed a Technical Expert Committee whose interim report recommended a ten-year moratorium on field trials — which the government rejected as inconclusive. On 23 July 2024 two judges split on the conditional approval of engineered mustard but agreed unanimously that the government must produce a national policy on engineered crops, through consultation with experts and state governments, within four months. A contempt application followed, alleging the policy was not made and releases went ahead anyway. What this case demonstrates is a court substituting itself for a regulator for two decades, and the limits of that: isolation distances and detection thresholds are enforceable orders, a national policy is not.

19.00000,-33.45000.name: The Quagga Project
19.00000,-33.45000.state: Elandsberg Farms, Western Cape, South Africa
19.00000,-33.45000.desc: Begun in 1987 by a museum taxidermist who had remounted a quagga foal in 1969 and kept tissue from it, which later allowed the DNA work showing the quagga was not a separate species but a subspecies of the plains zebra. On that basis the project selectively bred southern plains zebras for reduced striping and a browner body, drawing founder stock from as far as Zululand and Namibia. Within four generations animals were born whose coat pattern closely resembles museum specimens. The regulatory outcome is the part that could not have been predicted: the agriculture minister declared the rebred animal, named the Rau quagga after the project's founder, a landrace breed under the Animal Improvement Act. A recovered wild phenotype was recognised by the state not as a restored subspecies but as a breed of livestock, which is the same legal category the back-bred European cattle occupy — arrived at independently on another continent.
